## Context

Sprint 8 issue #29 introduced the `ObjectStorage` abstraction (boto3 + MinIO). New DB rows store opaque keys (e.g. `abc123_model.stl`). Pre-existing rows store legacy filesystem paths (e.g. `data/uploads/abc123_model.stl`).

`url_for()` in `services/object_storage.py` detects both forms transparently, but this is a temporary backward-compat shim with a `# TODO` marker.

See also: QENG-16855 (Jira)

## Work required

- Write an Alembic migration (or a standalone script) that reads every `uploaded_file_path` and `uploaded_image_path` value from `print_requests`, and every `qr_code` value from `inventory.items`
- For each legacy-path row: copy the file to object storage, update the DB row to the opaque key
- Remove the path-detection branch from `LocalFilesystemStorage.url_for()` and `S3CompatibleStorage.url_for()` once migration is confirmed
- Migration must be idempotent (safe to re-run)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All rows store opaque object-storage keys (no path separators)
- [ ] `url_for()` backward-compat branch removed
- [ ] Migration is idempotent and documented
- [ ] TODO comments in `services/object_storage.py` resolved

## Labels

`slice:data-migration` `phase:4`
title: QENG-16846: [Phase 4] Migrate legacy upload/QR filesystem paths to object-storage keys

## Goal Resolve the four deferred accessibility findings from PR #114 (portal design system audit, [#103](https://github.com/adc-quality/lab-tech-portal/issues/103)). PR #114 shipped the global token system + CSS-token extractions; this issue tracks the follow-on template migrations and a11y patches it explicitly deferred. ## Background PR #114 ([merged 2026-05-14](https://github.com/adc-quality/lab-tech-portal/pull/114)) completed the in-scope items from #103 (audit findings, FW design-system snapshot, `:root` token extraction, `--muted-text` darkening). Findings 4, 5, 6, and 9 from that PR were called out as **follow-on work**: - **Finding 4 — Dark mode status pills**: hardcoded status hex values in `jira_import.html`, `systems_dashboard.html`, `system_form.html` don't adapt to dark mode (amber `#d97706` on dark card is ~3.2:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1). The `--status-active-color` / `--status-warning-color` / `--status-error-color` / `--status-neutral-color` tokens already exist in `:root` and `.dark-mode` (added by PR #114); this issue migrates the three templates to use them. - **Finding 5 — No skip-to-main link**: keyboard users tab through 6 toolbar stops on every page. Add `Skip to main content` as the first focusable element, visible only on focus. - **Finding 6 — No `
` landmark on toolbar**: `.toolbar-links` divs should be `
`. Single base-template change. - **Finding 9 — Responsive breakpoint for 7-column Jira-import table**: only one breakpoint at 720px; Jira-import table is unusable on tablets between 720–1024px. Add a 1024px breakpoint that hides/stacks lower-priority columns. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `jira_import.html`, `systems_dashboard.html`, `system_form.html` use the four `--status-*-color` tokens instead of hardcoded hex (light + dark mode both ≥ WCAG AA 4.5:1) - [ ] Skip-to-main-content link added to `base.html`, becomes focusable on first Tab, jumps focus to `
` (or equivalent landmark) - [ ] `.toolbar-links` containers rendered as `
` - [ ] Jira-import table responsive at 720–1024px (column priority defined; lowest-priority columns hidden or stacked) - [ ] Manual a11y check with browser screen reader on at least one page: skip-link works, nav landmark announced, status pills readable in dark mode ## Out of scope - Architecture-guide pattern file `frontend/design-system-for-flask-templates.md` — that lives in `qe-architecture-ai-assisted-guide`; file there as a separate issue if/when prioritized. - Broader breakpoint/responsive overhaul — only Jira-import in scope here because that's the table flagged in finding 9. ## References - PR #114 body (findings list): https://github.com/adc-quality/lab-tech-portal/pull/114 - Originating issue: #103 (closed as shipped by #114) ## Size: S | Priority: P3

## Goal

Validate that the Docker Compose stack sustains ≥50 concurrent users without `database is locked` errors surfacing under WAL + Gunicorn workers + Celery worker sharing one SQLite file. Required by [docs/CLEANUP_PLAN.md:218](docs/CLEANUP_PLAN.md) (risk-hotspots) and Verification step 4 ([docs/CLEANUP_PLAN.md:303](docs/CLEANUP_PLAN.md)).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Load-test tool selected (locust or k6) and committed to repo
- [ ] Scenario covers a mixed read/write workload across all 5 tools: Inventory, RF Chamber, Checkout, System Locator, Print Requests
- [ ] Baseline run at 50 concurrent users for 10 minutes — zero `database is locked` errors, p95 latency documented per endpoint
- [ ] Results checked into `docs/load-test-baseline.md` with date + commit SHA
- [ ] If failures surface, file follow-up issue and accelerate D-part2 (PostgreSQL migration) per risk-hotspots mitigation

## Technical Details

Tool recommendation: locust (Python-native, fits the stack).
Config: `locustfile.py` in `tests/load/` with one TaskSet per tool.
Run via: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.load.yml up`

Mix targets (rough):
- 60% reads (list/detail views)
- 30% writes (POST forms)
- 10% Jira-touching writes (print-request submit, system-locator import)

## Files to Create

- `tests/load/locustfile.py`
- `docker-compose.load.yml`
- `docs/load-test-baseline.md`

## Dependencies

- Slice G-part1 complete (Sprint 6, done)

## Story Points

5

## Testing

- [ ] Run baseline locally, capture results
- [ ] Re-run after each Slice D-part2 milestone to track improvement
